previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with multiple comorbidities, including morbid obesity, diabetes, congestive heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and obstructive sleep apnea, was admitted for a planned split-thickness skin graft to treat a non-healing right lower extremity wound sustained two weeks prior. She underwent successful debridement and grafting, with a wound vacuum placed postoperatively. Her recovery was complicated by a transient rise in creatinine to 1.6 on postoperative day 3, which resolved spontaneously without intervention, and a brief episode of left-sided chest pain that was ruled out for cardiac ischemia. The graft remained intact, and she was mobilized on postoperative day 6. She was discharged to extended care with instructions for wound care, activity progression, and follow-up in two weeks for staple removal. At discharge, she was afebrile, hemodynamically stable, and in good condition.

Brief Hospital Course:
PATIENT
___ year old female hx of COPD, dCHF, OSA, obesity 
hypoventilation syndrome coming in with hypoxia, AMS, ___, and 
UTI. She was admitted to the ICU secondary to her hypotension 
(systolic 90's), hypoxia (sat 70's on RA) and AMS. 

ACUTE ISSUES
# HYPOXIA: Patient was noted to not be on home 2 L NC on 
admission to hospital, and subseuqently when placed on 2 L NC in 
ICU quickly hit goal saturation > 88 %.

# AMS: On initial presentation, it was noted her AMS was likely 
multifactorial   (hypoxia with concomitant UTI, with delerium 
superimposed on baseline dementia). She was given haldol 
sparingly for episodes of acute agitation, was treated for UTI 
as below and was frequetnly reoriented to self and place. 
Benzodiazpeines were avoided. Narcotics were not restarted until 
patient transferred to floor and was fully oriented and returned 
to baseline mental status.
 
# UTI: For her UTI, patient has history of multiple ESBL urinary 
tract infections and presented with positive UA on admission. 
She was started on empiric meropenem, and blood and urine 
cultures were pending at time of transition to floor. Urine 
cultures grew ESBL E. coli, so continued on meropenam while in 
house. PICC line placed at discharge and patient sent out to 
complete a total of two week antibiotic therapy with ertapenam. 

# ___: For her ___, she had a Cr of 3.9 on admission with 
baseline 0.9-1.1. Her FeUrea 5.3% in house was suggestive of 
pre-renal etiology. Patient's UOP was monitored in the ICU. 
Renal U/S sound was completed when patient transferred to the 
floor - demonstrated no signs of hydronephrosis or sludging as a 
causal factor. Serum creatinine 1.0 at time of discharge.

# dCHF: For her Acute exacerbation of dCHF, Pt had pulmonary 
edema on CXR on admission, with BNP at 981 ( was 84 3 months 
prior), elevated JVP and bilateral ___ edema. EKG was without 
obvious ischemic changes. Cardiac enzymes were trended in house 
and patient was set for a goal of -1 L per day with IV lasix 
boluses, which she achieved. Her symptoms and mental status 
improved with diuresis.  
She was discharged to the floor on ___ with plan to continue 
gentle diuresis, follow-up on urine and blood cultures and 
narrow antibiotics appropriately, and to continue monitoring of 
her respiratory function which had much improved. On the floor 
was converted to home torsemide and she continued to have 
approprite diuresis. Discharged home without alteration in home 
dose of diuretics.

Discharge Weight: 133.4 kg

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# Bradycardia: Patient had intermittent episodes of bradycardia 
while sleeping, likely due to OSA. HD stable and assymptomatic. 
No intervention 
# COPD: Initially treated as COPD flare in ED, but treatment 
discontinued once admitted. Continued home inhalers/nebs
# OSA/obesity hypoventilation syndrome: Patient not home CPAP 
and refused while inpatient. 
# Elevated CK: Trended inpatient and downtrended without
